artiest/rocky-roberts.text:
Rocky Roberts, in full Charles Roberts, was born in 1940 in Tanner, Alabama, and died in 2005 in Rome. He was an American R&B singer who later became an Italian citizen. He served in the United States Navy, where he was a boxing champion. His interest in singing arose when he heard the country musician Doug Fowlkes and his band on board ship, who let him sing along.

When he won a singing contest in Juan-les-Pins in France while on leave, he stayed in Europe after leaving the navy in 1962. He appeared on the French television show Les raisins verts. In 1965 Renzo Arbore and Gianni Boncompagni invited him to Rome to record the signature tune of their radio programme Bandiera Gialla. That was T-Bird, a hit in Italy, and after that he went on living in Rome.

In 1967 he had a big Italian hit with Stasera mi butto, which won the Festivalbar. The success led to a film of the same title in which he starred himself, and more Italian films followed. He almost always wore sunglasses. Roberts also sang the title song of the 1966 film Django, written by Luis Bacalov. Quentin Tarantino used that recording again in 2012 as the opening music of Django Unchained. In this way his voice has remained known far beyond Italy.
artiest/rocky-roberts.listen: Listen to his Django and notice the voice, which is heavy and soulful, and the orchestra, which heightens the drama of the western.

artiest/rod-stewart.text:
Rod Stewart is a British singer and songwriter, born in 1945 in Highgate in north London. His career began in 1962, when he played harmonica as a street musician. He then sang in various groups, and in 1967 he joined the Jeff Beck Group. In 1969 he became the singer of Faces and also began a solo career with the album An Old Raincoat Won't Ever Let You Down.

His breakthrough was Every Picture Tells a Story in 1971, with the single Maggie May. Never a Dull Moment followed, with You Wear It Well, and after the end of Faces in 1975 the album Atlantic Crossing with the ballad Sailing. Later records such as A Night on the Town, Foot Loose & Fancy Free and Blondes Have More Fun produced hits such as Tonight's the Night, You're in My Heart and Da Ya Think I'm Sexy? Later he carried on with softer rock and in the 2000s recorded songs from the Great American Songbook. His trademark is a raspy voice. He was knighted in 2016.

Stewart began as a raw rock singer with influences from folk, soul and rhythm and blues. With Da Ya Think I'm Sexy?, a song with disco sounds, he showed that even a rock singer could reach the dance floor. That makes him, in the course, an example of the transition from rock to pop at the end of the 1970s.
artiest/rod-stewart.listen: Listen to Maggie May and notice the raw voice and the acoustic guitar and mandolin. Compare that with the tight, danceable rhythm of Da Ya Think I'm Sexy?

artiest/rod-temperton.text:
Rod Temperton, in full Rodney Lynn Temperton, was an English musician, songwriter and producer, born in 1949 in Cleethorpes in Lincolnshire. As a boy he played drums and after school worked in a fish factory before becoming a keyboard player in dance bands. That took him to Worms in Germany. In 1974 he answered an advertisement in Melody Maker and became the keyboard player of the funk band Heatwave. There he wrote songs such as Boogie Nights, Always and Forever and The Groove Line. In 1978 he left the band to concentrate on writing.

The producer Quincy Jones heard his work and in 1979 brought him in for Michael Jackson's album Off the Wall. Temperton wrote, among other things, Off the Wall and Rock with You for it. For Thriller from 1982 he wrote three songs, including the title track, and also the spoken words for Vincent Price. He also wrote for George Benson (Give Me the Night), for Patti Austin and James Ingram (Baby, Come to Me), for Donna Summer and for the Brothers Johnson. His colleagues praised him as highly disciplined: he had every detail on paper before he came into the studio.

Temperton mostly stayed out of the spotlight, but his songs defined the sound of soul, funk and disco in the late 1970s and early 1980s. In the course he is the writer of Rock with You, a supple disco song with a soft, precise voice.
artiest/rod-temperton.listen: Listen to Rock with You by Michael Jackson and notice the soft vocals, the smooth bass and the strings. How relaxed does the rhythm sound, and how precise are the small details?

artiest/rodgers-en-hammerstein.text:
Rodgers and Hammerstein was the writing duo of the composer Richard Rodgers and the lyricist Oscar Hammerstein II. Together in the 1940s and 1950s they wrote a series of American musicals that changed the genre. Rodgers wrote the music, Hammerstein the lyrics and the story of the songs. Their first joint musical was Oklahoma! from 1943, followed by, among others, Carousel, South Pacific and The King and I. The last of these was filmed in 1956, with Rita Moreno in a supporting role.

Their musicals use songs to tell the story. The music grows out of the scene and the characters, and light songs stand alongside serious subjects. The music is melodic and easy to sing, and many songs became known far beyond the theatre.

Their last joint work was The Sound of Music, with a book by Howard Lindsay and Russel Crouse based on the book by Maria von Trapp. The musical premiered on Broadway in 1959, with Mary Martin and Theodore Bikel, and won five Tony Awards, including for best musical. Hammerstein died nine months after the premiere. In 1965 a film followed with Julie Andrews and Christopher Plummer, which won five Oscars. In this way the duo stands at the foundation of the American musical tradition, on which later writers continued to build.
artiest/rodgers-en-hammerstein.listen: Listen to My Favorite Things from The Sound of Music. Notice how the song is a list of small things and how the melody keeps repeating with small changes.

artiest/roger-daltrey.text:
Roger Daltrey is an English singer and actor, born in 1944 in London. He is a co-founder and the singer of The Who, the rock band with the guitarist Pete Townshend, the bassist John Entwistle and the drummer Keith Moon. His powerful voice and strong stage presence made him one of the best-known frontmen in rock.

With The Who he sang, among others, My Generation, Pinball Wizard, Won't Get Fooled Again, Baba O'Riley, Who Are You and You Better You Bet. In 1973 he also began a solo career, with albums such as Daltrey, Ride a Rock Horse and Under a Raging Moon. His solo hits include Giving It All Away, Without Your Love and Under a Raging Moon. He also acted in films and in the theatre. In 1990 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of The Who, and in 2025 he was knighted for his work for music and charity.

The Who is regarded as one of the most influential rock groups of the twentieth century. The group gave expression to the anger and unrest of a young generation, and Daltrey gave that a voice. In the course his name appears in the description of the four members, in the chapter on youth cultures between 1950 and 1980.
artiest/roger-daltrey.listen: Listen to My Generation and notice how Daltrey stutters the lines. How does that fit the angry tone of the song?

artiest/roger-sessions.text:
Roger Sessions was born in 1896 in Brooklyn and died in 1985 in Princeton. He was an American composer, teacher and writer on music. He began at Harvard at the age of fourteen, then studied with Horatio Parker and Ernest Bloch at Yale and taught at Smith College. He wrote his first major works mainly during a stay in Europe. An exception is the incidental music for The Black Maskers from 1923.

His style changed over the course of his life. Until about 1930 he wrote in a more or less neoclassical manner. Between 1930 and 1945 his music became tonal but harmonically complex. From 1946 he wrote atonally and, beginning with the Solo Violin Sonata from 1953, serially. His friendship with Arnold Schoenberg influenced him, but he adapted the technique: he used rows for the melodic themes and wrote the remaining parts freely.

Sessions was also an influential teacher, including at Princeton, Berkeley and the Juilliard School. He wrote books such as Harmonic Practice in 1951 and The Musical Experience of Composer, Performer, Listener. He was friends with Schoenberg and Thomas Mann. In 1974 he received a special Pulitzer Prize for his life's work, and in 1982 the Pulitzer Prize for music for his Concerto for Orchestra, performed in 1981 by the Boston Symphony Orchestra. He belongs to the American composers who linked the postwar avant-garde to tradition in a voice of their own.
artiest/roger-sessions.listen: Listen to the first minutes of his Concerto for Orchestra and notice how the motifs are passed between different instruments, even when the sound is sharp and dissonant.

artiest/roger-troutman.text:
Roger Troutman was an American singer, musician, writer and producer, born in 1951 in Hamilton, Ohio. He grew up as the fourth of nine children and played in various small bands with his brothers. In 1979 George Clinton discovered him and signed his group Zapp to Uncle Jam Records. He then signed with Bootsy Collins to Warner Bros. The debut Zapp came out in 1980, with More Bounce to the Ounce, produced by Collins. In the 1980s more albums followed, and hits such as Dance Floor and Computer Love.

Troutman was known for his talk box, a device connected to an instrument. He used an Electro Harmonix Golden Throat, first with a Minimoog and later with a Yamaha DX100. In this way he made a synthesizer sound like a singing, robotic voice. As a soloist he had a first number one on the R&B chart in 1981 with his funk version of I Heard It Through the Grapevine, and in 1987 I Want to Be Your Man reached number three on the Hot 100. He also produced for others, including Shirley Murdock.

In the 1990s he worked with hip-hop artists such as Snoop Dogg and 2Pac. In 1995 he appeared on California Love by 2Pac and Dr. Dre, which topped the American Hot 100. His music was sampled heavily and formed a foundation for West Coast hip-hop. In the course his talk box is central to G-funk: slow funk grooves with a singing synthesizer.
artiest/roger-troutman.listen: Listen to California Love and notice the singing, robotic voice that weaves through the lyrics. That is Roger Troutman's talk box.

artiest/rogier-van-otterloo.text: Rogier van Otterloo, son of the conductor Willem van Otterloo, was an arranger and conductor with Dutch broadcasting and in light music. In the 1970s he became the regular composer for Paul Verhoeven. For Turks Fruit (1973) he wrote a melancholy score in which Toots Thielemans's harmonica plays a leading role. Keetje Tippel (1975) and Soldaat van Oranje (1977) followed, with a large orchestra and a heroic main theme. Van Otterloo brought the sound of the broadcasting orchestra, with strings, jazz soloists and light pop influences, to the Dutch feature film. He died in 1988 at the age of 46.
artiest/rogier-van-otterloo.listen: Notice the melodic solos, such as the harmonica in Turks Fruit, above a warm, broad arrangement for orchestra.

artiest/romanos-de-melode.text:
Romanos the Melodist lived in the sixth century and was a Byzantine poet and composer of hymns. He was born at the end of the fifth century in Emesa in Syria, into a Jewish family. As a boy he was baptised. Later he became a deacon in Beirut and moved to Constantinople. He was still alive after 555. Little is known about his life; most of it comes from the Menaion for October.

According to a legend, he initially could not read or sing well. During the vigil before Christmas around the year 518 he is said to have read so badly that someone else had to take his place. Afterwards, so the legend goes, he received the gift of singing and poetry in his sleep. How much of that is true cannot be verified.

His name is linked to the kontakion, a form of rhymed sermon that is set to music. Such a poem has several stanzas with the same metre and a recurring refrain, preceded by a prelude in a different metre. The rhythm is based on accents. Romanos used vivid language, sharp comparisons and dramatic dialogues. According to tradition he wrote more than a thousand hymns. Eighty-nine are attributed to him, of which some sixty are generally regarded as genuine. His Kontakion of the Nativity is regarded as his masterpiece. In the Eastern Orthodox Church he is the patron saint of music, and his work also influenced Armenian hymns.
artiest/romanos-de-melode.listen: Find a recording of the Kontakion of the Nativity and listen to the refrain that keeps returning. Notice the unaccompanied singing in a single line.

artiest/ron-carter.text: Ron Carter from Michigan first studied cello and classical double bass, but found that there was little room for a Black bassist in the orchestras of the time. He switched to jazz. From 1963 to 1968 he played in the second quintet of Miles Davis, with Herbie Hancock and Tony Williams. That rhythm section played freely and flexibly, and could change tempo and mood in the middle of a piece. Carter is the bassist who has played on the most jazz records; the Guinness Book of Records named him in 2015 the most recorded jazz bassist. In 1991 he played on The Low End Theory by A Tribe Called Quest.
artiest/ron-carter.listen: Follow the bass: it holds the beat, but constantly changes direction.

artiest/ron-goodwin.text:
Ron Goodwin was born in 1925 in Plymouth and died in 2003. He was an English composer and conductor who became known above all for his film music. He learned piano and trumpet at an early age, formed a band of his own at school, Ron Goodwin and the Woodchoppers, and studied trumpet at the Guildhall School of Music in London. In 1943 he became a copyist and arranger at the music publisher Campbell, Connelly and Company, and later also for the BBC.

In the 1950s he arranged and conducted hundreds of recordings for more than fifty artists, including Petula Clark and Jimmy Young, which produced more than a hundred hits. At the same time he released records of his own with Ron Goodwin and his Concert Orchestra and wrote music for documentaries. He wrote his first feature film score in 1958. When Lawrence P. Bachmann became a producer at MGM British Studios in 1959, Goodwin was given the music for most of those films.

He wrote music for more than seventy films in a career of more than fifty years. Well known are Where Eagles Dare, Battle of Britain, 633 Squadron, the Miss Marple films with Margaret Rutherford, and Frenzy. His style is orchestral, melodic and full of tension, suited to adventure and war films. In the 1980s he concentrated on live concerts and appeared as a guest conductor with, among others, the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra.
artiest/ron-goodwin.listen: Listen to the main theme of 633 Squadron and notice the brass and the rhythmic drive that seems to propel the aeroplanes.

artiest/ron-grainer.text: Ron Grainer (1922–1981) was born in Australia and moved to England in 1952. There he became one of the best-known writers of television themes. In 1963 he wrote the theme for Doctor Who. Delia Derbyshire of the BBC Radiophonic Workshop turned that score into sound, with individual notes from oscillators and processed tapes, without a single ordinary instrument. It was one of the first television themes made entirely electronically. Grainer wanted to credit her as co-composer, but the BBC did not allow it. He then wrote the theme for The Prisoner (1967) and the film music for The Omega Man (1971).
artiest/ron-grainer.listen: In the Doctor Who theme, listen to the pulsing bass line and the floating electronic melody, both made with oscillators and tape.

artiest/ron-hardy.text:
Ron Hardy was born in 1958 and died in 1992. He was a DJ and producer from Chicago and a key figure in early house music. He began in 1974 at the gay club Den One, where, with two turntables, a mixer and a tape recorder, he played long nights of underground dance music. Around 1977 he worked in Los Angeles. In late 1982, when Frankie Knuckles left the Warehouse, Hardy played at that club's new venue, which later became The Music Box. In 1986 he made his first recording with Chip E.: Donnie by The It.

His style differed sharply from that of Knuckles. Knuckles played smoothly, while Hardy played with manic energy and little regard for sound quality. He mixed classic Philadelphia disco records with Italo disco, new wave and rock, pitched the records up much faster than usual and sometimes played tracks backwards. He used a lot of tape edits and kept adjusting the sound system. The Music Box was known for its enormous volume.

Chicago producers such as Marshall Jefferson, Larry Heard, Adonis, DJ Pierre and Chip E. often let Hardy hear their new music first. That is how the wild, squelching sound of a Roland TB-303 bass line by Phuture also came to him. Well after his death he came to be seen as an innovator of edits and mixes of disco, soul, funk and early house.
artiest/ron-hardy.listen: Listen to Donnie by The It and notice the electronic rhythms and the vocals. This is how you hear the beginning of house, as Hardy played it in the club.

artiest/ronald-bruner-jr.text:
Ronald Bruner Jr. was born in 1982 and is an American drummer, composer and producer. He played, among others, in Suicidal Tendencies, a hardcore punk and crossover thrash band. He is also a fixture in the jazz of Los Angeles. He was part of The Stanley Clarke Band, which won a Grammy in 2010 for best contemporary jazz album.

Bruner comes from a musical family. He is the older brother of Stephen Bruner, better known as Thundercat, and of Jameel Bruner, who also performs as Kintaro. He regularly plays with Thundercat, Kamasi Washington and his cousin Terrace Martin, as a member of the Los Angeles collective West Coast Get Down. In 2015 he could be heard with that collective on The Epic, Washington's debut on a major label. His own album Triumph appeared in 2017.

His drumming style combines the power of punk and thrash with the freedom of jazz. In this way he fits a new generation of Los Angeles musicians who blend jazz, funk, hip-hop and rock without boundaries.
artiest/ronald-bruner-jr.listen: Listen to a track from The Epic by Kamasi Washington and focus on the drums. Notice how they push the ensemble forward and how they play around the beat.

artiest/roni-size.text:
Roni Size is the stage name of Ryan Owen Granville Williams, born in 1969 in Bristol to Jamaican immigrants. Reggae was one of his early influences. He was expelled from school at sixteen and went to parties of the Bristol sound system The Wild Bunch, a forerunner of Massive Attack. He learned the basics of producing in a community centre, with turntables, a mixing desk, drum machines and samplers. Later he built a studio of his own.

Together with Krust, Suv and DJ Die he founded Full Cycle Records; Full Cycle and Dope Dragon followed in 1993. His first releases appeared in 1994 on V Recordings. By 1997 he was known as the founder and figurehead of Roni Size & Reprazent, a drum and bass group with the singer Onallee, the MC Dynamite MC, a bassist and a drummer, who played live. Their debut album New Forms was released in 1997, with singles such as Brown Paper Bag and Heroes. It won the Mercury Prize.

On the second album, In the Mode, in 2000, Zack de la Rocha and Method Man sang along. In 2002 came his first real solo album, Touching Down. In 2008 he brought Reprazent back together and performed at major European festivals. In this way he took drum and bass from the British clubs to a wide audience and showed that the music could be played live.
artiest/roni-size.listen: Listen to Brown Paper Bag and notice the double bass, the fast drums and Onallee's vocals. Can you hear that the band is playing live?

artiest/roni-size-reprazent.text:
Roni Size / Reprazent is a British drum and bass group formed around the producer Roni Size, in everyday life Ryan Williams, from Bristol. He founded the group so that he could also play live the tracks he made in the studio. The first live performance followed in April 1997 at the Tribal Gathering festival. The group included members of his label Full Cycle, among them Krust, DJ Die and DJ Suv, who stood behind their equipment, with the singer Onallee, the MC Dynamite MC, the bassist Si John and the drummer Clive Deamer on stage.

The debut album New Forms was released in June 1997. Singles came out with Onallee's voice, such as Brown Paper Bag, Heroes, Share the Fall and Watching Windows. The album went five times platinum and in 1997 won the Mercury Prize, a special recognition for a dance group. In 2000 In the Mode followed, with guests such as Rahzel, Zack de la Rocha of Rage Against the Machine and Method Man. In later years the group played at major festivals, including Glastonbury and Coachella, and together with an orchestra and choir at the reopening of Colston Hall in Bristol.

The group's hallmark is that drum and bass is also played live. Alongside the driving jungle rhythms we hear real drums and an upright bass, and the music blends influences from hip-hop, funk, soul and house. The Guardian called Brown Paper Bag a masterpiece that piles up layers of melody and rhythm and then breaks them down again. With this album an electronic style moved from the underground into the mainstream of British pop music.
artiest/roni-size-reprazent.listen: Listen to Brown Paper Bag and notice the drums, which go very fast, and the calm double bass playing beneath them. Notice too how Onallee's voice floats softly above the frantic beat.

artiest/ronnie-flex.text:
Ronnie Flex is the stage name of Ronell Langston Plasschaert, born in 1992 in Rotterdam. He is a rapper, singer and producer, of Surinamese and Moluccan descent, and grew up in Capelle aan den IJssel. At fourteen he began making tracks and not long afterwards he wrote raps. He attended the pop academy at Zadkine, but did not finish it.

In 2012 he won a State Award for Rookie of the Year and signed with the label Top Notch. His first EP, Tankstation, appeared in 2013. With Zusje and Pocahontas he built an audience, and in 2014 his debut album De nacht is nog jong, net als wij voor altijd came out. He collaborated a lot with others. With Lil' Kleine he made Drank & Drugs and Zeg dat niet, and with Jonna Fraser and others Liegen voor de rechter. He also belonged to the collective New Wave, which received the Popprijs 2015 in 2016. Later came the albums Rémi in 2017 and NORI in 2018.

His music combines rap with singing and a melodic, electronic production, often with a light and danceable atmosphere. He was regarded as the most successful rapper of all time in the Dutch Top 40. He also appeared on television, including in It Takes 2 and The Masked Singer, and in 2018 worked with BLØF on the song Omarm me.
artiest/ronnie-flex.listen: Listen to Zusje and notice how he raps and sings by turns. Can you hear how the melody stays in your head in the choruses?

artiest/ronnie-spector.text:
Ronnie Spector was born in 1943 as Veronica Bennett in East Harlem, New York, and died in 2022. In the late 1950s she formed the vocal group The Ronettes with her sister Estelle and her cousin Nedra Talley. In 1963 they signed to Phil Spector's label Philles, and he produced the majority of their recordings. That began a series of hits in the 1960s: Be My Baby in 1963, Baby, I Love You in 1963, (The Best Part of) Breakin' Up and Do I Love You? in 1964 and Walking in the Rain in 1964.

In 1965 the Ronettes were voted the third vocal group in England, behind the Beatles and the Rolling Stones. In 1966 they opened for the Beatles, although Ronnie had to stay at home because of Phil. She married Phil Spector in 1968 and after that hardly performed. In 1972 she left their home and in 1974 she filed for divorce.

Her first solo album, Siren, appeared in 1980. In 1986 she became known again through Take Me Home Tonight, a duet with Eddie Money. After that she made, among others, Unfinished Business, Something's Gonna Happen and English Heart. In 1990 her memoir Be My Baby was published. As a Ronette she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2007. Her voice, powerful and with a slight tear in it, gave the girl-group music of the 1960s a raw edge, and her image as the bad girl of rock 'n' roll made her a model for later female singers.
artiest/ronnie-spector.listen: Listen to Be My Baby and notice the drums that open the song. Can you hear how her voice lifts itself above the thick wall of sound of the orchestra?

artiest/ronny-jordan.text:
Ronny Jordan was the stage name of Robert Laurence Albert Simpson, a British guitarist, born in London in 1962. He died in 2014. He was part of the acid jazz movement at the end of the twentieth century. He himself called his music urban jazz, a mixture of jazz, hip-hop and R&B.

His breakthrough came when he was featured on Jazzmatazz, Vol. 1 by the rapper Guru in 1993. In 1992 his debut album The Antidote appeared, with an acid jazz arrangement of So What by Miles Davis, which became a worldwide hit. After that came, among others, The Quiet Revolution in 1993, Light to Dark in 1996 and A Brighter Day in 2000, which received a Grammy nomination for best contemporary jazz album. In 1994 he also appeared on the album Stolen Moments: Red Hot + Cool, in aid of the Red Hot Organization. He received a MOBO award for best jazz act and a Gibson award for best jazz guitarist.

His guitar playing is soft and melodic, often with a warm tone that recalls the classic jazz guitarists, but now over hip-hop beats and funk rhythms. His track The Jackal reached a wider audience when the actress Allison Janney lip-synced it in The West Wing. In this way he brought jazz to an audience that came to it via clubs, hip-hop and R&B.
artiest/ronny-jordan.listen: Listen to his version of So What and compare it with the original by Miles Davis. Notice the beat beneath the guitar and how the melody remains recognisable.

artiest/rory-storm-and-the-hurricanes.text:
Rory Storm and the Hurricanes was an English band from Liverpool. The singer and leader was Rory Storm, the stage name of Alan Caldwell, born in 1938 in Liverpool. His father was a window cleaner. Storm worked as a cotton salesman before he started a skiffle group. In 1958 he opened the Morgue Skiffle Club in the cellar of a large Victorian house, where, besides his own group, the Quarrymen, the later Beatles, also played.

In their day the Hurricanes were among the most popular groups in the clubs of Liverpool and Hamburg. On record the success failed to materialise. In the early 1960s they released only two singles, and neither made the charts. The second and last single was a version of America from West Side Story, produced by Brian Epstein, the manager of the Beatles. Storm stuttered, but that did not hamper his singing. He died in 1972.

The band is historically important above all because of its drummer. Ringo Starr played with the Hurricanes before he joined the Beatles in August 1962, replacing Pete Best. The two groups already knew each other from Hamburg. The Hurricanes show how big the Liverpool scene was, with many groups who knew one another and sometimes exchanged a musician.
artiest/rory-storm-and-the-hurricanes.listen: Look up a recording by the Hurricanes, for example their version of America, and listen to the guitars and the drums. Can you hear how the band sounds like a hard-hitting live act from the clubs of Liverpool and Hamburg?

artiest/roscoe-mitchell.text: The saxophonist Roscoe Mitchell from Chicago was one of the first members of the AACM. In 1966 he recorded Sound, the first album by an AACM musician. Besides saxophone and trumpet, it features bells, whistles, harmonica and silence. His group grew into the Art Ensemble of Chicago, with the trumpeter Lester Bowie, the saxophonist Joseph Jarman and the bassist Malachi Favors; later the drummer Famoudou Don Moye joined. Mitchell plays all the saxophones, from soprano to bass, and also writes for orchestra. He taught for years at Mills College in California.
artiest/roscoe-mitchell.listen: Hear how small instruments and silences are just as important as the saxophone.

artiest/roscoe-mitchell-sextet.text:
The Roscoe Mitchell Sextet is the group with which the saxophonist Roscoe Mitchell recorded the album Sound in 1966. Mitchell was born in 1940 in Chicago. As a boy he played saxophone and clarinet, and his brother Norman introduced him to jazz. In 1965 he was one of the first members of the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians, the AACM, an organisation of Chicago musicians who wanted to make new music.

On Sound, Mitchell, the trumpeter Lester Bowie, the tenor saxophonist Kalaparusha Maurice McIntyre, the bassist Malachi Favors, the trombonist Lester Lashley and the drummer Alvin Fielder played. The album departed from the exuberant free jazz of New York, partly because the group used unusual sounds and silences. It is an early document of the Chicago avant-garde.

From this circle grew the Art Ensemble of Chicago, which performed under that name from 1969 and between 1969 and 1971 lived and played in Europe. Mitchell later founded, among others, the Creative Arts Collective, the Sound Ensemble and the Note Factory and also worked in classical music. Critics call him a key figure in avant-garde jazz. The music of the sextet demands attentive listening: space, small sounds and sudden outbursts stand side by side.
artiest/roscoe-mitchell-sextet.listen: Listen to the album Sound and notice the silences between the sounds. Can you hear how the musicians also use small instruments and unusual sounds?

artiest/rosenberg-trio.text:
The Rosenberg Trio is a Dutch jazz trio from the Sinti community. The group consists of the lead guitarist Stochelo Rosenberg, the rhythm guitarist Nous'che Rosenberg and the bassist Nonnie Rosenberg. Nous'che and Nonnie are sons of Sani Rosenberg, a musician from the Dutch Sinti. They grew up in a very musical family, in which the music of Django Reinhardt set the standard. Nous'che was already playing together with his cousin Stochelo when Stochelo was about ten years old. Nonnie was encouraged to play the double bass and studied it hard until he had mastered the instrument. An exact founding date is not known, but the trio has been playing under this name since about 1989.

Their first album was Seresta, followed by, among others, Gypsy Summer and Impressions. In 1992 the live album Live at the North Sea Jazz Festival appeared, on which the trio can be heard at its youthful peak. Later they played with Stéphane Grappelli, Biréli Lagrène and Peter Beets, and made the album Roots and the homage Tribute to Stéphane Grappelli. In 2010 the DVD Djangologists appeared, in which Reinhardt was commemorated. All three members have been appointed Knight in the Order of the Netherlands Lion.

The style is called jazz manouche or gypsy swing. Two guitars play fast and rhythmically over a driving bass, without drums, with fast solos full of ornamentation. Stochelo plays a Selmer guitar with an oval sound hole, the model Reinhardt himself used. The trio showed that Reinhardt's tradition lived on in the Netherlands and that it sounds full of energy to a new audience as well.
artiest/rosenberg-trio.listen: Listen to Minor Swing and notice the two guitars: one plays the melody and solos at lightning speed, the other holds the song together with its rhythmic strumming. Can you hear that no drums are needed to make it swing?

artiest/roswell-rudd.text:
Roswell Rudd was born in 1935 in Sharon, Connecticut, and died in 2017 in Kerhonkson, New York. He was an American trombonist and composer. He studied at Yale, where in the mid-1950s he played in Eli's Chosen Six, a student band in the exuberant traditional jazz style. That band recorded two albums, one of them for Columbia. What he learned there with rags and stomps he carried into his later collaborations with Archie Shepp, Cecil Taylor, John Tchicai and Steve Lacy.

From 1962 he worked a great deal with Shepp. In the 1960s he could be heard on free jazz recordings, such as those of the New York Art Quartet, the soundtrack of the 1964 film New York Eye and Ear Control and the album Communications by the Jazz Composer's Orchestra. He also played with Don Cherry, Larry Coryell, Pharoah Sanders and Gato Barbieri. With Lacy he recorded the music of Thelonious Monk.

Rudd was also an ethnomusicologist. He taught the subject at Bard College and the University of Maine and for decades worked on and off for Alan Lomax on his projects Cantometrics and Global Jukebox. In 2000 and 2001 he travelled to Mali, which led to the 2001 album MALIcool with the kora player Toumani Diabaté. In 2005 he recorded Blue Mongol with the Mongolian Buryat Band. In this way he linked the trombone of jazz with music from all over the world.
artiest/roswell-rudd.listen: Listen to a recording by the New York Art Quartet and notice the trombone, which now roars and then sounds like a Dixieland player. Can you hear the tradition beneath the freedom?

artiest/rotterdam-termination-source.text:
Rotterdam Termination Source is a Dutch gabber and hardcore group from Rotterdam formed around the producer Maurice Steenbergen, at first together with Danny Scholte. The duo is regarded as one of the pioneers of Dutch gabber house fury. It began around 1991 and released on Rotterdam Records, the label that Paul Elstak founded in 1992 and which is regarded as the first hardcore label in the world.

The biggest hit was Poing, from 1992. The track is almost bare: a hard, stomping beat with one characteristic sound, the poing, that keeps returning. There is not much more to it than that, and precisely that simplicity made it so effective on the dance floor. It became a hit in the Netherlands and Denmark and also entered the British chart. The football supporters of West Bromwich Albion are said to have based their Boing Boing chant on it. In 1993 came the Christmas record Merry X-Mess, which also made the chart in Great Britain, and more EPs appeared later. In 2007 a jumpstyle version of Poing was released.

The music belongs to the first years of Dutch hardcore: hard, fast and tongue in cheek. Poing showed that a track built from one sound and one rhythm could be enough to carry a whole country along. Steenbergen later worked, among other things, on Paul Elstak's music videos.
artiest/rotterdam-termination-source.listen: Listen to Poing and count how often the poing sound returns. Notice how little changes in the track and how the beat keeps driving forward all the same.

artiest/rowwen-heze.text:
Rowwen Hèze is a Dutch band from America, a village in northern Limburg, which sings mainly in the dialect of that region. The band emerged in 1985 from The Legendary Texas Four, which was looking for a new singer. Jack Poels, who had previously sung in the band Bad Edge, took the place on condition that he could do one song in dialect. The name refers to Christiaan Hesen, a wilful village character from America nicknamed Rowwen Hèze, loosely translated as rough Hesen. In the early years the group mainly played English-language covers, but more and more songs came in the dialect.

National fame came through a carnival song, Niks stront niks, from 1987. A 1988 demo with Bestel mar became a big hit a few years later. In 1990 the band signed with a record company, and in 1992 it played Pinkpop for the first time. In 1993 it was the first Dutch band at the Roskilde Festival. Albums such as Boem, Station America and Zondag in 't zuiden followed. Since 1991 the core has consisted of Poels, William van Enckevort, Jan Philipsen, Theo Joosten, Jack Haegens and Martîn Rongen. The traditional annual tent tour ends with the Slotconcert in America.

The music blends folk, brass band and Tex-Mex, with influences from The Pogues and Los Lobos. The lyrics are about ordinary things: a hangover, the local brass band, fatherhood or a village character. Rowwen Hèze also reaches people who do not fully understand the dialect and shows that a local language can touch a large audience in Dutch pop music.
artiest/rowwen-heze.listen: Listen to Bestel mar and notice the instruments you would not expect in an ordinary rock band, such as accordion and wind instruments. Hear how the voice sounds in Limburgish and how cheerfully the music trots along.

artiest/roxanne-shante.text:
Roxanne Shanté is the stage name of Lolita Shanté Gooden, born in 1969 in Queens, New York. She was a member of the Juice Crew and became known in 1984 through the Roxanne Wars. That year she spoke at the Queensbridge housing complex with Mr. Magic and Marley Marl, who were talking about U.T.F.O. That rap group had failed to show up for a concert, and their B-side Roxanne, Roxanne had in fact become a hit.

Shanté was asked to write an answer from the perspective of the Roxanne in that song. Marley Marl turned the instrumental version of Roxanne, Roxanne into the beat for Roxanne's Revenge. It became a hit at once and made her, at fourteen, one of the first popular female MCs. The Roxanne Wars followed, a series of answer records, and she went on tour with Marley Marl. In 1985 Round One, Roxanne Shanté vs Sparky Dee came out, with her battle against the rapper Sparky D. In 1988 she rapped on Loosey's Rap by Rick James. Bad Sister followed in 1989 and The Bitch Is Back in 1992.

By around the age of twenty-five she had largely withdrawn from the record industry, but she continued to make guest appearances and mentored young female rappers. In 2008 Roxanne's Revenge was number 42 on VH1's list of the hundred greatest hip-hop songs. In 2017 the film Roxanne Roxanne about her life appeared. She showed that a girl could win in hip-hop through pure rapping skill.
artiest/roxanne-shante.listen: Listen to Roxanne's Revenge and notice her tempo, her tone and the way she answers U.T.F.O. directly.

artiest/roxette.text:
Roxette was a Swedish pop duo of the singer Marie Fredriksson and the singer and songwriter Per Gessle. They had been friends for years and were both well known in their own country: Fredriksson with Swedish-language solo albums, Gessle as the singer of the band Gyllene Tider. In 1986 their record company EMI suggested recording an English-language song together. Gessle translated one of his songs, and so Neverending Love became the first single. The name Roxette came from a song by Dr. Feelgood. The debut album Pearls of Passion appeared that same year.

The international breakthrough came in a striking way. An American exchange student took the second album, Look Sharp! (1988), home with him and gave it to a radio station in Minneapolis. The Look became a radio hit there before the record was on sale in America, and in April 1989 the song topped the American chart. Listen to Your Heart followed, then It Must Have Been Love from the film Pretty Woman (1990) and Joyride (1991), which also reached number one in the Netherlands. The album Joyride became their best-selling record.

Roxette made guitar pop with catchy choruses, alternating with big power ballads in which Fredriksson's powerful voice took centre stage. Gessle wrote most of the songs. After Fredriksson's brain tumour in 2002 the duo lay dormant for a long time; in 2009 they came back with a world tour. Fredriksson died in 2019. After ABBA, Roxette is the best-selling music act from Sweden, and thus a link in the long Swedish tradition of pop songs that were sung all over the world.
artiest/roxette.listen: Listen to The Look and notice how the song is built from short, separate phrases and a tight guitar riff. Hear how Gessle and Fredriksson divide the vocals.

artiest/roxy-music.text:
Roxy Music was an English rock band, started in London in 1970 by the singer and keyboard player Bryan Ferry and the bassist Graham Simpson. The saxophonist and oboist Andy Mackay answered an advertisement and brought along his friend Brian Eno, who was not a musician but could operate a synthesizer and a tape recorder. The drummer Paul Thompson and the guitarist Phil Manzanera completed the group. The name came from old cinemas: Roxy had something of faded glamour, and Music was a pun on rock music.

In 1972 the debut album Roxy Music appeared, and shortly afterwards the single Virginia Plain, which reached number four in England. The performance on Top of the Pops, with striking costumes, made the band one of the faces of glam rock. After For Your Pleasure (1973) Eno left; Eddie Jobson took his place with keyboards and electric violin. Stranded (1973), Country Life (1974) and Siren (1975), with Love Is the Drug, followed. After a break the band came back with Manifesto (1979) and Flesh + Blood (1980). The last album was Avalon (1982), smoother and calmer than the early work.

Roxy Music combined nostalgia and the music of the future: Ferry's crooner voice, Mackay's saxophone and oboe, Eno's electronic sounds and tight rock drums. The band gave glam rock an artistic side, influenced early British punk and was a model for much new wave. That is why it is no coincidence that in the clubs of the 1980s people danced to Roxy Music, alongside Bowie and Kraftwerk.
artiest/roxy-music.listen: Listen to Virginia Plain and notice how the saxophone, the piano and Eno's shrieking synthesizer play through one another. Hear too how the song ends: it has no ordinary chorus and stops fairly abruptly.

artiest/roy-ayers.text:
Roy Ayers was born in 1940 in Los Angeles into a family of musicians. His father played trombone and his mother piano. At the age of five he received his first vibraphone mallets from Lionel Hampton. He grew up in South Park, in the centre of the Black music scene of Southern California, and attended Thomas Jefferson High School, where Dexter Gordon had also been a pupil. In 1962 he began recording as a bebop sideman. In 1963 his debut album West Coast Vibes appeared. In 1966 he joined the band of the flautist Herbie Mann.

In the early 1970s he formed his own band Roy Ayers Ubiquity. The name means that something is everywhere at the same time. He made the acclaimed soundtrack for the 1973 film Coffy with Pam Grier. After that he moved from jazz-funk to R&B, as on Mystic Voyage from 1975 and on Everybody Loves the Sunshine from 1976. That last song became his best known, alongside Running Away and Freaky Deaky. In 1977 he also produced an album by the group RAMP.

Ayers is one of the pioneers of jazz-funk and was an important figure in acid jazz. He was called the Godfather of Neo Soul. Rappers have sampled his music so often that for a time he was among the most sampled artists. He died in 2025.
artiest/roy-ayers.listen: Listen to Everybody Loves the Sunshine by Roy Ayers. Notice the soft vibraphone, the loose bass line and the relaxed vocals, which together create a warm, summery atmosphere.

artiest/roy-eldridge.text: The trumpeter Roy Eldridge from Pittsburgh was, in the 1930s, the bridge between Louis Armstrong and Dizzy Gillespie. He learned fast lines by copying Coleman Hawkins's saxophone solos on the trumpet, and took over Armstrong's big tone and drama. His playing was fierce, fast and reached into the highest register. He played with Fletcher Henderson and led a band of his own in Chicago. In 1941 he became a soloist in Gene Krupa's big band, as one of the first Black musicians in a white band, where he recorded Let Me Off Uptown with the singer Anita O'Day. The young Dizzy Gillespie learned his solos by heart.
artiest/roy-eldridge.listen: Hear how the trumpet plays high and fast, with the fierceness of a saxophone.

artiest/roy-hargrove.text: Roy Hargrove from Texas was discovered as a schoolboy by Wynton Marsalis and came to New York via Berklee. He was counted among the Young Lions and named trumpeters such as Clifford Brown and Freddie Hubbard as models. With the Cuban group Crisol he won a Grammy in 1998 for Habana. With the RH Factor he blended jazz with soul, funk and hip-hop, and he played on albums by D'Angelo and Erykah Badu. He also remained a committed hard bop trumpeter. He died in 2018 at the age of 49.
artiest/roy-hargrove.listen: Hear how the trumpet swings as easily as it plays over a soul groove.

artiest/roy-orbison.text:
Roy Orbison was an American singer, writer and guitarist, born in 1936 in Vernon, Texas. He was given a guitar by his father at the age of six and grew up with country music and western swing. As a teenager he sang in a country band. In 1956, at the urging of Johnny Cash, he signed with Sam Phillips's Sun Records, where his first recording, Ooby Dooby, sounded like the early recordings of Elvis Presley. His greatest success came at Monument Records. Between 1960 and 1966 twenty-two of his singles reached the American top forty.

He wrote or co-wrote almost all his big hits, such as Only the Lonely in 1960, Running Scared and Crying in 1961, In Dreams in 1963 and Oh, Pretty Woman in 1964. His songs have intricate structures and dramatic ballads, with a powerful, high voice. He performed almost without movement, in black clothes, with dyed black hair and dark sunglasses. After the mid-1960s his career stalled because of personal tragedies, but he came back in the late 1980s. In 1988 he was a co-founder of the Traveling Wilburys, with George Harrison, Bob Dylan, Tom Petty and Jeff Lynne. He died in December of that year.

Orbison let vulnerability be heard at a time when male singers mainly wanted to seem strong. In the course he appears as an example of the slow style in which John Lennon at first wrote Please Please Me.
artiest/roy-orbison.listen: Listen to Only the Lonely and notice how the voice glides from low to high, and how the song becomes more and more tense. What does the singing do to the emotion?

artiest/royal-philharmonic-orchestra.text:
The Royal Philharmonic Orchestra is a symphony orchestra in London. The conductor Thomas Beecham founded it in 1946, having already founded the London Philharmonic Orchestra in 1932. In 1946 he reached an agreement with the Royal Philharmonic Society, so that his new orchestra could bear the name Royal Philharmonic. It also became the house orchestra of the Glyndebourne Festival and obtained lucrative recording contracts. The first rehearsal was on 11 September 1946, and the first concert four days later in Croydon. Within two years the orchestra had already made more than a hundred recordings.

After Beecham's death in 1961 the orchestra ran into difficulties. Rudolf Kempe became principal conductor and in 1970 received the title of conductor for life. He was succeeded by Antal Doráti, and later Walter Weller and André Previn, among others, followed. In the mid-1960s a report by the Arts Council saved the orchestra's future, and it has received subsidy ever since. The orchestra developed a sound of its own, especially in the woodwinds.

In 1981 the orchestra was in the Dutch Top 40 with Hooked on Classics, a medley of well-known classical pieces with a solid beat. In 2004 it gained its first permanent home in London at Cadogan Hall. It also plays at the Royal Festival Hall and the Royal Albert Hall and has given concerts abroad. Since 2021 Vasily Petrenko has been its music director. The orchestra also takes part in pop recordings and film music, and so shuttles between the concert hall and popular culture.
artiest/royal-philharmonic-orchestra.listen: Listen to Hooked on Classics and notice the continuous beat beneath the classical melodies. Can you hear how the fragments keep flowing seamlessly into one another?

artiest/roza-eskenazi.text: Roza Eskenazi was born around 1895 into a Sephardic Jewish family in Constantinople. She made her first recordings in 1929 and became the queen of rebetiko, with songs in the Smyrna style, full of Turkish and Greek melodies. During the German occupation she helped resistance fighters and Jews to go into hiding. In the 1970s she was rediscovered and inspired singers such as Haris Alexiou.
artiest/roza-eskenazi.listen: Listen to Ouzo Hasis from 1934: violin and santouri play together with her voice, which circles freely and playfully around the melody.

artiest/ruben-blades.text:
Rubén Blades was born in 1948 in Panama City. He is a singer, composer, actor, activist and politician and plays mainly salsa and Latin jazz. He studied political science and law in Panama. In 1970 he made his American debut with the album De Panamá a New York by the orchestra of Pete Rodriguez. In 1974 he moved to the United States, where he started in the mailroom of Fania Records and began working with Ray Barretto and Larry Harlow. The collaboration with the trombonist Willie Colón followed.

His first real hit was Pablo Pueblo on the 1977 album Metiendo Mano. In 1978 he wrote El Cantante, which Héctor Lavoe recorded and which gave him his best-known song. The 1978 album Siembra by Blades and Colón became the best-selling salsa album ever, with Pedro Navaja as its best-known song. Tiburón from 1981 protested against American interventions in Latin America. In 1984 he moved to Elektra and formed his band Seis del Solar, with the album Escenas. He also collaborated with Elvis Costello and Linda Ronstadt.

Blades brought lyrical depth to salsa, dance music with stories about daily life and politics. He also acted in films such as Crossover Dreams and later in Fear the Walking Dead. In 1994 he made a bid for the presidency of Panama and received 17 per cent of the vote. In 2004 he became minister of tourism.
artiest/ruben-blades.listen: Listen to Pedro Navaja from Siembra and follow the story in the lyrics. Notice how the band supports the story of the street character.

artiest/rudolf-friml.text:
Rudolf Friml was born in 1879 in Prague and died in 1972 in Los Angeles. He was a Czech-American composer of operettas, musicals, songs and piano music, and also a pianist. He entered the Prague Conservatoire in 1895, where he studied piano and composition with Antonín Dvořák. In 1901 he was sent away because he had performed without permission. After that he was the pianist for the violinist Jan Kubelík, with whom he toured the United States twice. In 1906 he settled there permanently, and in 1904 he had performed his own Piano Concerto in B flat major at Carnegie Hall.

His breakthrough as a theatre composer came in 1912 with The Firefly, an operetta that Victor Herbert had dropped. The show ran in New York for months. High Jinks, Katinka and You're in Love followed. He wrote his greatest successes in the 1920s, with Rose-Marie from 1924 and The Vagabond King. Both were successful on Broadway and in London and were filmed. His music is romantic and melodic, with above all European operetta traditions.

Friml went on composing and giving concerts well into his nineties. The Donkey Serenade from the film version of The Firefly, The Mounties and Indian Love Call are still played, often as parody. In Japan Song of the Vagabonds is known. He was one of the first members of the Songwriters Hall of Fame. In this way he formed a bridge between European operetta and the American musical.
artiest/rudolf-friml.listen: Listen to Indian Love Call from Rose-Marie and notice the big, singing melody. Can you hear how romantic and theatrical it sounds?

artiest/rudolf-werthen.text:
Rudolf Werthen is a Belgian violinist, conductor and teacher. He was born in Mechelen and was taught by André Gertler and Henryk Szeryng. In 1971 he was a laureate, with seventh prize for violin, of the Queen Elisabeth Competition. In 1985 he sat on its jury himself. Since 1975 he has taught at the Royal Conservatoire of Ghent.

Werthen is the founder and artistic director of the orchestra I Fiamminghi. In 1989 he was principal conductor of the symphony orchestra of the Flemish Opera. With I Fiamminghi he recorded, among other things, Le quattro stagioni in 1986, and cello concertos in 1987 and 1994, as well as the album Fratres. His discography runs from 1981 to 2006 and is broad: it contains music by the Latvian composer Peteris Vasks, by Takemitsu and by contemporary composers, and also Tango - La elegia de quienes ya no estan from 1999. That shows that he did not restrict himself to the standard repertoire but also performed new and lesser-known music.

His significance lies in his work as an orchestra leader and teacher in Flanders. He belongs to the conductors who brought the repertoire of the twentieth century and contemporary music to the concert hall and the record.
artiest/rudolf-werthen.listen: Listen to a recording by I Fiamminghi under Werthen, for example Fratres. Notice how long the sounds of the strings are sustained and how slowly the music changes.

artiest/rufus-thomas.text:
Rufus Thomas was born in 1917 in Cayce, Mississippi, and died in 2001 in Memphis. He was a singer, songwriter, dancer, DJ and comedian. He began as a tap dancer and vaudeville performer, appeared in travelling tent shows and in the Rabbit Foot Minstrels and for more than twenty years kept working by day in a textile factory. In the 1940s he wrote and sang his own songs. In 1951 he became a DJ at the radio station WDIA in Memphis, where he presented the afternoon programme Hoot and Holler.

In 1953, at the suggestion of Sam Phillips, he recorded Bear Cat for Sun Records, an answer to Hound Dog by Big Mama Thornton. It became the label's first national hit. Later he became a regular at Stax Records. In 1959 he recorded a duet with his sixteen-year-old daughter Carla Thomas, which began her career. His greatest successes were dance records, such as The Dog and Walking the Dog in 1963, Do the Funky Chicken in 1969 and (Do the) Push and Pull in 1970. The recordings are funky, playful and full of jokes.

He remained active into the 1990s and was known as The World's Oldest Teenager. In 1988 he took part in the Stax reunion and appeared in films such as Mystery Train. He was the father of Carla and Vaneese Thomas and of the keyboard player Marvell Thomas. In this way he stands between the rhythm and blues of the 1950s and the funk of the 1970s.
artiest/rufus-thomas.listen: Listen to Walking the Dog and notice the dog imitations and the bass. Can you hear how he takes the audience along in the dance?

artiest/rumon-gamba.text:
Rumon Gamba was born in 1972 and is a British conductor. He studied music at the University of Durham and conducting at the Royal Academy of Music in London, with, among others, Colin Metters, George Hurst and Colin Davis. He was the first conducting student to gain the DipRAM, the academy's highest diploma for performers. In 1998 he won a prize at the Lloyds Bank BBC Young Musicians Conductors Workshop and became assistant conductor of the BBC Philharmonic, later associate conductor.

He then led orchestras in Europe. From 2002 to 2010 he was principal conductor and music director of the Iceland Symphony Orchestra, from 2009 of NorrlandsOperan in Sweden, from 2011 of the Aalborg Symphony Orchestra and from 2022 of the Oulu Symphony Orchestra. He conducted at English National Opera and in 2011 led the world premiere of Two Boys by Nico Muhly. In 2014 he conducted all nine of Beethoven's symphonies in Umeå, each preceded by a new work.

Gamba made more than fifty CDs for Chandos, including the series on film music. With the BBC Philharmonic he recorded works by Miklós Rózsa, Richard Addinsell, Malcolm Arnold, Bernard Herrmann, Erich Wolfgang Korngold and Ralph Vaughan Williams. In this way he contributed to the recognition of film music as orchestral repertoire.
artiest/rumon-gamba.listen: Listen to a recording of film music by Gamba with the BBC Philharmonic, for example by Korngold. Notice how the orchestra tells a scene with sound alone.

artiest/run-dmc.text:
Run-DMC was a hip-hop group from Hollis, a neighbourhood in Queens, New York. The three members grew up there together: Joseph Simmons (Run), Darryl McDaniels (DMC) and Jason Mizell, the DJ who called himself Jam Master Jay. Run was the younger brother of Russell Simmons, who was then the manager of the rapper Kurtis Blow. In 1983 Russell helped them get a record deal. The first single, It's Like That/Sucker MCs, was an instant success.

Run-DMC sounded different from the hip-hop that came before. Instead of disco and funk grooves there were hard, bare drum machine beats, scratches by Jam Master Jay and two rappers who shouted the lines at each other. The debut Run-D.M.C. (1984) included Rock Box, with a rock guitar beneath the raps. Its video was the first hip-hop video on MTV. King of Rock (1985) and Raising Hell (1986) followed. The latter album included Walk This Way, a new version of the Aerosmith song, with Steven Tyler and Joe Perry joining in and Rick Rubin as producer. It became one of the best-known songs in both hip-hop and rock.

In their clothing, too, they broke with the old style. No more glitter and leather, but Kangol hats, leather jackets and Adidas shoes without laces, as on the street. Run-DMC was the first hip-hop group with a gold and a platinum album, and performed at Live Aid. With the Beastie Boys, LL Cool J and Public Enemy they ushered in the new school of hip-hop. In 2009 they were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/run-dmc.listen: Listen to Walk This Way by Run-DMC and Aerosmith. Notice how the two rappers shout the lines in turn, and how Joe Perry's guitar riff cuts through the bare drum beat.
